issue.body:
## About
#### The PR's size
Making many separate PRs would have been good for the ability to review them. I had that ambition initially but realized that making many PRs each affecting a lot of files and the same files over and over was hard and I gave up on that, I'm hoping it won't cause too much trouble - sorry in advance!

## In this PR
I have aimed make the `.yaml` consistent in various ways.

- [x] Labels (using helper)
- [x] Selectors (using helper)
- [x] Block indentation (`nindent` introduced)
- [x] List element indentation
- [x] Whitespace chomp left (`{{- }}`)
- [x] Template function (`include` replace `template`)
- [x] Yaml and Helm comments (`#` vs `{{/* */}}`)
- [x] Passing scope (with `merge (dict "key1" "val1") .`)
- [x] Utilize [`helm lint`](https://docs.helm.sh/helm/#helm-lint)

- [x] Setup values for `yamllint` (`lint-chart-values.yaml`)
- [x] Utilize [`kubeval`](https://github.com/garethr/kubeval)

- [x] Update guidelines (`CONTRIBUTING.md`)
- [x] Consider dynamic .yaml in [chartpress](https://github.com/jupyterhub/chartpress)
- [x] Consider dynamic .yaml in [pod culler](https://github.com/jupyterhub/zero-to-jupyterhub-k8s/tree/master/images/pod-culler)
- [x] Consider dynamic .yaml in [kubespawner](https://github.com/jupyterhub/kubespawner) ([kubespawner#159](https://github.com/jupyterhub/kubespawner/issues/159), [kubespawner#161](https://github.com/jupyterhub/kubespawner/pull/161))

## Related

#538 #622 #624 [helm#3811](https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/pull/3811) [helm#3470](https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/issues/3470) [helm#3837](https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/pull/3837) [helm#3854](https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/issues/3854) [kubespawner#159](https://github.com/jupyterhub/kubespawner/issues/159) [kubespawner#161](https://github.com/jupyterhub/kubespawner/pull/161)

body:
Still an issue in v2.8.2. I followed the code, this is the trace for reference.

https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/blob/be1e974cccec4f5583ef6e67b229f35f9e6edd2e/pkg/chartutil/files.go#L168-L179

Apparently `toYaml(...)` within Helm is a wrapper function around [`github.com/ghodss/yaml`](https://github.com/ghodss/yaml) `yaml.Marshal(...)`. I could confirm that the added new line comes from that functions return value by running the code below. But `github.com/ghodss/yaml` in actually also wrapping a function in [`gopkg.in/yaml.v2`](https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml) which has the actual cause of the new line we want to abolish.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/ghodss/yaml"
/* ghodss/yaml utilizes the following yaml package, using that directly gives us the same result.
	"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
*/
)

type Person struct {
	Name string `json:"name"` // Affects YAML field names too.
	Age  int    `json:"age"`
}

func main() {
	p := Person{"Erik", 31}
	y, _ := yaml.Marshal(p)
	fmt.Println(string(y))
	fmt.Println(string(y))
	/* Output:
	age: 31
	name: Erik

	age: 31
	name: Erik

	*/
}
```

### Solution 1
Trim away the new line within Helm toYaml wrapper function.

### Solution 2 (Not happening)
Figure out how to avoid adding new line within [`gopkg.in/yaml.v2`](https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml) and hope it makes sense for them to update their code to do so, then hope for that update to propegate to [`github.com/ghodss/yaml`](github.com/ghodss/yaml), and finally propegate into a Helm release.

I made an issue, I got help to conclude it did not make sense for them to update the behavior to not include a new line. See [go-yaml/yaml issue #355](https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml/issues/355).


### Solution 3
![hqdefault](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3837114/38341453-e340611c-3878-11e8-98e6-bd6876ad9322.jpg)

---

I vote for Solution #1 :)

issue.title: yaml.Marshal(...): adds an (for me) unwanted \n

repository.name: yaml
repository.description: YAML support for the Go language.

body:
### Solution 4 (Not happening)
Find a way to make the whitespace chomping work on the new line outputted by the toYaml, that would be the best solution I think! Why does that not work!?

### Update 1
So why does [Go text/template](https://godoc.org/text/template#hdr-Text_and_spaces) not chomp toYaml output? I think it might be because toYaml outputs a newLine followed by indentation whitespace!

### Update 2
Everything that is outputted by evaluating `{{ }}` will be hands off for the `go text/template` whitespace chomping. For example if you would write `{{if true}}{{ print "This ends with new lines\n\n" }}{{- end }}` you still have the new lines.

__Conclusion__
This solution suggestion won't happen, as it would suddenly expect the go text/template whitespace chomping to invade outputs of other `{{ }}`.

issue.body:
## Summary

`toYaml` is currently introducing a new line, and since the new line it is part of a functions output, it can't be whitespace chomped away but requires a `trimSuffix "\n"`. This commit trims one trailing `\n` from the toYaml output by default as it [seems like the best solution when considering options](https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/issues/3470#issuecomment-378785908).

The PR fixes #3470 and #3410.

## About the new line

```yaml
# values.yaml
myKeys:
  key1: value1
  key2: value2
```

__Situation 1__
A new line is added by toYaml...
```yaml
# my-template.yaml
keys:
  {{- toYaml .Values.myKeys | nindent 2 }}
other:
  irrelevantKey: irrelevantValue

# my-template.yaml (parsed)
keys:
  key1: value1
  key2: value2
  
other:
  irrelevantKey: irrelevantValue
```

__Situation 2__
Okay so we could compensate by not adding another new line after the toYaml output? Well... Then you might get indentation failures instead, this would only work if the next yaml statement was supposed to be indented to the same level as the toYaml content.
```yaml
# my-template.yaml
keys:
  {{- toYaml .Values.myKeys | nindent 2 -}}
other:
  irrelevantKey: irrelevantValue

# my-template.yaml (parsed)
keys:
  key1: value1
  key2: value2
  other:
  irrelevantKey: irrelevantValue
```

__Situation 3__
This works, but it is quite cluttered. Perhaps we can make it built in instead? Hence this PR.
```yaml
# my-template.yaml
keys:
  {{- toYaml .Values.myKeys | trimSuffix "\n" | nindent 2 }}
other:
  irrelevantKey: irrelevantValue

# my-template.yaml (parsed)
keys:
  key1: value1
  key2: value2
other:
  irrelevantKey: irrelevantValue
```

## About toYaml
There are two implementations of toYaml.

https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/blob/be1e974cccec4f5583ef6e67b229f35f9e6edd2e/pkg/chartutil/files.go#L168-L179

https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/blob/1a55161a53345816d724e1df9664f789113e1328/pkg/strvals/parser.go#L32-L40

issue.body:

Output of `helm version`:

Output of `kubectl version`:
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"10", GitVersion:"v1.10.1", GitCommit:"d4ab47518836c750f9949b9e0d387f20fb92260b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2018-04-12T14:26:04Z", GoVersion:"go1.9.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}

```

Cloud Provider/Platform (AKS, GKE, Minikube etc.): bare metal

Installing `stable/prometheus` chart is broken on helm `2.9.0`. Works fine in helm `2.8.2`
The prometheus configMap entry contains broken yaml for the `prometheus.yml` key.

Specifically, the `alerting:` section that is added by `templates/server-configmap.yml` is missing a new line and results in the following snippet being generated

```
      - action: replace
        source_labels:
        - __meta_kubernetes_pod_name
        target_label: kubernetes_pod_namealerting:
      alertmanagers:
      - kubernetes_sd_configs:
```

which should actually be like this

```
      - action: replace
        source_labels:
        - __meta_kubernetes_pod_name
        target_label: kubernetes_pod_name
    alerting:
      alertmanagers:
      - kubernetes_sd_configs:
```

Possibly related to #3410 #3470 as referenced in the 2.9.0 release notes

This results in the prometheus server pod failing to starts as it complains about malformed yaml as shown below

```
level=error ts=2018-04-27T04:41:05.546416253Z caller=main.go:582 err="Error loading config couldn't load configuration (--config.file=/etc/config/prometheus.yml): parsing YAML file /etc/config/prometheus.yml: yaml: line 202: mapping values are not allowed in this context"
level=info ts=2018-04-27T04:41:05.546496152Z caller=main.go:584 msg="See you next time!"
```

body: We've reverted this change due to breaking the Prometheus charts that expected this behaviour. Because this is expected behaviour we cannot change this, so we're gonna have to keep this one closed as intentional for Helm 2, but keep it open for Helm 3.

So far I've managed to workaround this issue by calling `trim` on the `toYaml` output.
By doing something like this:
```
{{- range $i, $vol := .Values.volumes }}
        - name: {{ $vol.name }}
{{ toYaml $vol.path | trim | indent 10 }}
{{- end }}
```

I got the following output:
```
volumes:
        - name: log-volume
          hostPath:
            path: /var/log/foo
        - name: process-comm
          hostPath:
            path: /tmp/process/foo
        - name: config-volume
          configMap:
            name: foo-config
```

My current practice, that I'm quite happy with, is to write...

```yaml
something:
  {{- .Values.somethingElse | toYaml | trimSuffix "\n" | nindent 2 }}
```

trimSuffix resolves this issue, nindent instead of indent adds a new line before the content and that combined with a whitespace left chomp makes the indentation of the template code look good as well.
